title: Build a small command-line tool from scratch (Python)
prompt:
Create a command-line tool `wordfreq.py` in this folder using only the Python 3 standard library.

Usage: `python wordfreq.py FILE [--top N]`

- It counts the words in FILE. Counting is case-insensitive (output words in lowercase). A word is a run of letters, digits or apostrophes, so "don't" is one word.
- It prints the N most frequent words (default 10), one per line, formatted as `<word> <count>`, sorted by count (highest first) and then alphabetically (plain string order, so digits come before letters).
- If FILE does not exist, it prints an error message to stderr and exits with status 1.

Also write unit tests in `test_wordfreq.py` (unittest) and make sure they pass.
